newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Nov building sinks 1.4 pct from yr before.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Nov building sinks 1.4 pct from yr before.

text.p: The real value of work carried out by registered Mexican construction companies fell 1.4 percent in November compared with the same month in 1995, Mexico's statistics institute INEGI said Tuesday.
Declines in construction were led by a drop in transportation and electricity projects by 41.2 percent for November from the same period the previous year.

"It should be noted that this figure was influenced by a very high level observed in 1995, when construction companies began a large number of telephone line installation projects. Work at the end of 1996 was already near completion," INEGI said in a statement.
Construction value for housing projects also sank during the time period by 11.6 percent, the institute said.

The real value of work rose in November from the previous year for transportation projects 15.8 percent, for petroleum and petrochemical projects 14.2 percent, for other construction 12 percent and for water and sanitation projects 9.3 percent.
Mexico's construction companies bought 17.6 percent more materials, and hired 11.4 percent more people in Nov. 1996, compared with the same month in 1995, the institute said.
